title: The Impact of Personal Budgeting Skills on College Students' Financial Stability
authors: Dela Torre, J.M.Y.; Jangao, J.P.P.; Maghilum, J.T.; Man-onan, R.J.H.; Pepito, S.G.; Rapirap, G.P.; Cervantes, J.Z.
venue: Research Journal in Business and Economics
tldr: Strong personal budgeting skills significantly enhance college students' financial stability, with 0.72 correlation between budgeting competency and financial well-being.
problem_and_motivation: College students increasingly face financial challenges due to rising living costs and economic uncertainties. Many lack adequate financial education and rely on informal knowledge sources, leading to poor financial behaviors. There is a need to understand how budgeting practices influence financial stability among students with limited allowances.
approach: Used descriptive-correlational research design with 213 randomly selected respondents from 457 enrolled students.
Administered structured questionnaire assessing budget planning, financial goal setting, and expense tracking.
Collected demographic information including age, sex, program, and average monthly allowance.
Analyzed data using descriptive statistics, Pearson R correlation, T-Test, and ANOVA with SPSS software.
Applied four-point Likert scale for measuring responses from Strongly Disagree to Strongly Agree.
findings: num: Correlation coefficient of 0.7247 with p<0.01 indicates strong positive relationship between budgeting skills and financial stability.
num: 86% of students had monthly allowance below ₱1,000, indicating significant financial constraints.
num: Mean budgeting skills score of 3.45 (Very High) across planning, goal setting, and tracking.
num: Mean financial stability score of 3.49 (Very High) across savings, stress, and expenses.
num: Significant differences observed across age, year, program, and monthly allowance groups.
key_figures_tables: Table 1: Demographic profile distribution → Majority are female (53%) with allowance below ₱1,000 (86%).
Table 2: Personal budgeting skills assessment → Students demonstrate Very High competency in all areas.
Table 3: Financial stability assessment → Students report Very High financial stability overall.
Table 4: Correlation analysis → Strong positive relationship (0.7247) between budgeting and stability.
Table 5: Demographic group differences → Significant variations across profile groups.

key_equations.explanation: Pearson correlation coefficient between budgeting skills and financial stability.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This study quantifies the relationship between personal budgeting skills and financial stability among Filipino college students. It demonstrates that budget planning, goal setting, and expense tracking significantly influence financial well-being. The research validates theoretical frameworks of financial planning behavior and self-control in a developing country context. Findings provide empirical evidence for implementing financial literacy programs in higher education institutions.
directly_justifies: Strong positive correlation (0.7247) exists between budgeting skills and financial stability.
Students with limited allowances demonstrate Very High budgeting competency.
Budgeting reduces financial anxiety and improves control over money management.
limits: Limited to one higher educational institution in Bukidnon, Philippines.
Relies on self-administered questionnaires with potential response bias.
Cross-sectional design does not capture changes over time.
Findings may not generalize to students with different socioeconomic backgrounds.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan of all topic domains identified high relevance for budgeting strategies (7.A), Filipino young professionals (1.A), and financial behavior (1.C) as core study components. Medium relevance for user-declared preferences (2.C), financial behavioral profiles (5.A), savings management (13.A), and evaluation frameworks (12.A) as supporting aspects. Low relevance for expense categorization (3.A), landscape of existing systems (4.A), mobile UX (9.B), and engagement dynamics (11.A) as contextual mentions. Domains related to predictive modeling, anomaly detection, and ML model serving were considered and rejected as not covered by this empirical budgeting study.
